_comment: Two-tier plan v3 stage B′ (docs/2026-09-18_two_tier_plan_v3.zh.md §5.2, rewritten 2026-09-20; decisions §6.2 D49–D60): the INSTRUCTION-vocabulary executor. Every arm is the stage A executor L60_D20 (D30: lookback 60 s = seq_len 30 at dt 2 s, segment Δ = 20 s = control_horizon_s, N1 = 2 segments, specific-force+path-angle + first-order lag, random remaining-path-uniform training anchors with the Δ future floor, 180 epochs, selection on the fixed-anchor common-grid ADE at L−1, split_seed 1337) with plan_conditioning = instruction: the executor is handed the four instruction words in force at the Δ/τ = 2 positions of its segment (the vocabulary artefact B0′ wrote — bins and thresholds under its sha; τ = 10 s, D54). ONE development cohort for every arm (D33 / D47: the grid's L60_D60 cohort, records ≥ 120 s: train 6853 / val 1404). ORDER (the user, 2026-09-20; plan §5.2.5): the SECOND LAYER FIRST. The queue trains the instruction prior per seed before anything else and with no gate — `--executor` is only the door to the cohort's split, so it reads the baseline's stage A checkpoint. Then it flies the baseline itself (the grid's L60_D20 checkpoints, protocol none, from L−1 on this cohort), then per configuration: train both seeds, fly each `--protocol truth-instruction` (the truth's words by flown position: the B1′ upper bound), and gate B1 (D57: both established shares not worse on both seeds, at least one metric beyond the grid's p75 seed line on both seeds, fully flyable ≥ 0.95). No records at train time ("predict": false): the readings are the closed loop's. B2′ (closed-loop fine-tuning) and B3′'s decoding protocols are not built yet and are not declared here. Arm keys: <configuration>_s<seed>.

L60_D20.what: the stage A executor L60_D20 — no token — flown protocol none from L−1 on the B cohort by this queue, with records; the baseline every configuration is judged against

I20.what: the instruction executor: L60_D20 with plan_conditioning = instruction on the τ = 10 s vocabulary (two positions per 20 s segment); read against the baseline's protocol-none reading on the same flights
